Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)

as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged

class: GalaxyUserTool

shell_command: |

    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

    format: tabular

chunk=get_range(size-65536,size-1)

CO/E and CO/L peaks are primarily regulated by OCT-SOX and KLF motifs as well as CTCF, TEAD, GRHL and ZIC motifs. However, different combinations of motifs are engaged at different time points across the time course via cooperative binding of OSK with other TFs that are expressed at specific time points.
